fields.name: PlayerId
fields.evidence: The only member: the writer bg3.exe+0x17FAAA0 (called from bg3.exe+0x17F5A30) allocates it with ComponentFrameStorageAllocRaw(storage, 4), initialises it with DAT_14617ceac (the Toolkit's DefaultConstructComponents EoCClient.dll+0x2CC8A0 writes *Unassigned_exref, the same 'unassigned id' constant) and then copies a 4-byte value queued for that entity (system +0x1A0 values, +0x1B0 entities). Live value 1 for the controlled character while eoc::user::ReservedForComponent of the same session holds the UserId 0x10001: so it is not a UserId but the local player number (1 = first local player). The Toolkit's ecl::InputController::IsInSelectorMode, which takes this component in its WorldView, resolves the player through Character::GetReservedForPlayerId and PlayerManager::GetPlayerCamera.

open_questions: The name: the 4-byte value is a local player number by its live value (1) and its readers (input, camera target, lightbar, sound per player), but no reader that compares it with a named PlayerId was read; the type of the Toolkit's 'Unassigned' constant was not established.
second_pass: Offset and width settled by the Windows writer bg3.exe+0x17FAAA0 (4-byte AllocRaw, default from the 'Unassigned' constant, then a queued 4-byte id); live 1 against ReservedFor's 0x10001 rules out a UserId, so it is written as an int32 player number.
